posts.content_md:
I was futzing with my sp-907 late this afternoon, putting a cooling fan in the box where it lives, and found that when I put it back in its box the power output had dropped to 15mW. I took it back out, tweaked the mirrors to 25mW and put it back in the box. Now I was down to 10mW.

I thought maybe resting one end on my desk and another on a chair might not have been the best arrangement for tweaking the power, done so I could get to all the alignment screws, so I propped it high on three supports and set about tweaking the power again. This time I couldn't get it above 19mW.

Grrrr.

I ended up discovering that the main tube appears not to be screwed down properly to the housing.

[](http://www.dragonseye.com/gallery/v/family/MichaelH/holography/laserhead1.jpg.html)

[](http://www.dragonseye.com/gallery/v/family/MichaelH/holography/laserhead2.jpg.html)

It's apparently been this way since I bought it and I never noticed until now.

Anyone know what size screws these are?

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md:
The tube mount looks OK to me. I mean the ballast tank mount. The plasma-tube is the small diameter tube that runs the whole length of the resonator, and its mounts are not shown in the pics. 

You might want to look between the resonator and heat shield, at both ends. The screws that hold the rubber feet on may be too long, and therefore putting a torque on the resonator. This will definately prevent optimum and/or consistant alignment (speaking from direct experience). 

I hope you're not running it laying sideways, like in the pics! That will certainly make it unstable. Anyway, I have a couple of dead heads as well. If you need spare parts, let me know.

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md:
Michael-

If you gently apply pressure with your fingers to the mirror mounts on the end while monitoring output power, you can determine if your laser needs alignment. You won't actually see any movement - it's on the order of fractions of a wavelength. If gently pushing, pulling, or twisting the mirror mounts results in an increase in output, then you could use an alignment. On the other hand, if no change is noted, your low output power is probably gas related.

I have a 107 that has heaters mounted to it. I suspect it is of slightly different construction from others, as it doesn't get up to full power until it has run for a few hours and is thoroughly warmed up. The diference between cold and hot is 20 mw vs 35mw. When it's cold, I can get more power by moving the mirrors with the above technique. When it's hot, the power only drops as I move the mirrors.
